items.content_html:
Agentic AI’s intersection with devices like phones, speakers and personal assistants hadn’t been visited much in the Prompt Economy. At least that was the case, up until last week when we heard from an upgraded Alexa+.

Amazon’s newly rebuilt Alexa+ represents a significant shift toward agentic AI, according to Wired. The article reports that Amazon redesigned Alexa around generative AI to move beyond scripted commands and toward autonomous task execution. This rearchitecture required solving complex integration challenges across tens of thousands of devices and services, as well as combining multiple large language models into a coordinated system capable of sustained, natural conversation. Wired notes that Amazon’s internal collaboration across AWS, Devices & Services, and its AGI teams gave Alexa+ the technical foundation to operate as a true digital assistant rather than a command-and-response interface.

Wired also highlights Amazon’s development of Nova Act, a visual-reasoning agent that enables Alexa+ to complete tasks on websites when APIs do not exist. This capability allows the assistant to navigate pages, fill out forms, and execute actions much like a human would, extending Alexa’s reach across the broader internet. Combined with a new multi-model orchestration system built on Amazon Bedrock, Alexa+ can evaluate multiple providers in real time, minimize latency, and carry a request through from intent to fulfillment. The article concludes by describing Amazon’s broader ambition for “ambient assistance,” in which Alexa+ becomes a background system that coordinates services seamlessly across a user’s digital life. 

And speaking of speaking into devices, last week was also notable for an Indian Express report that Chinese telecom company ZTE, in partnership with ByteDance, has introduced what may be the world’s first fully agentic AI smartphone, a prototype called the Nubia M153. Unlike current AI assistants that operate within limited app boundaries, this device integrates ByteDance’s Doubao model directly into the operating system, allowing the AI to see the phone’s screen, navigate apps, tap and type, make payments, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously. Demonstrations show the agent selecting the correct app for a job, completing forms, and finalizing bookings without user guidance. The article notes that this level of “full-stack control” over the smartphone represents a major leap beyond Samsung, Apple, and other global competitors, whose AI actions remain permission-gated and restricted to a narrow set of partner integrations.

According to the article, the phone’s capabilities rely on a hybrid architecture: cloud-based semantic reasoning performed by Doubao and on-device execution handled by Nebula-GUI, a 7-billion-parameter model trained by ZTE. This approach enables the agent to complete complex tasks such as booking hotels from a single photo, coordinating robotaxi trips across Baidu Apollo, or negotiating with other automated systems, such as Meituan’s delivery bots. The prototype also demonstrates deep app-level knowledge, OS-level visibility, and multimodal understanding, including identifying objects in the physical world and generating modified images.

The Indian Express concludes that while it is unclear whether the device will become commercial, it signals that the first true agentic smartphones may emerge not from Silicon Valley but from China’s integrated AI and mobile ecosystem. 

The Prompt Economy is also an active ecosystem for medical devices. HealthTech reports that agentic AI is emerging as a major new category of technology in healthcare. Unlike traditional generative AI, which relies on user prompts, agentic AI can synthesize information across systems, revisit prior steps, and proactively initiate follow-up actions. Experts cited in the article, including NVIDIA’s Amanda Saunders and UiPath’s Jason Warrelmann, note that while these agents remain forms of narrow AI rather than true general intelligence, they represent a significant shift in how healthcare organizations may manage clinical, administrative, and operational workflows. The article highlights rapid projected growth: Gartner expects one-third of enterprise applications to include agentic AI by 2028, and Market.us estimates the global market will near $200 billion by 2034.

The article outlines several high-value use cases across drug discovery, clinical trials, insurance operations, and patient care. Agentic AI can screen billions of compounds, identify eligible trial participants, generate and submit insurance appeals, recommend treatments, and serve as virtual health assistants that deliver instructions, reminders, and symptom-based escalations. Because these agents operate autonomously, HealthTech emphasizes the critical importance of data governance and oversight, including strict control over which systems agents may access and how protected health information is segmented. The article notes that many major technology vendors, including NVIDIA, Microsoft, IBM, Google, and UiPath, are already embedding agentic capabilities into their platforms, enabling health systems to adopt the technology through existing tools.

Ultimately, the publication frames agentic AI as a transformative but carefully managed step toward more automated, efficient healthcare operations.

items.title: In comedy of errors, men accused of wiping gov databases turned to an AI tool
items.summary: Defendants were convicted of similar crimes a decade ago. How were they cleared again?
items.content_html:
Two sibling contractors convicted a decade ago for hacking into US State Department systems have once again been charged, this time for a comically hamfisted attempt to steal and destroy government records just minutes after being fired from their contractor jobs.

The Department of Justice on Thursday said that Muneeb Akhter and Sohaib Akhter, both 34, of Alexandria, Virginia, deleted databases and documents maintained and belonging to three government agencies. The brothers were federal contractors working for an undisclosed company in Washington, DC, that provides software and services to 45 US agencies. Prosecutors said the men coordinated the crimes and began carrying them out just minutes after being fired.

Using AI to cover up an alleged crime—what could go wrong?

On February 18 at roughly 4:55 pm, the men were fired from the company, according to an indictment unsealed on Thursday. Five minutes later, they allegedly began trying to access their employer’s system and access federal government databases. By then, access to one of the brothers’ accounts had already been terminated. The other brother, however, allegedly accessed a government agency’s database stored on the employer’s server and issued commands to prevent other users from connecting or making changes to the database. Then, prosecutors said, he issued a command to delete 96 databases, many of which contained sensitive investigative files and records related to Freedom of Information Act matters.

items.title: QE Is Coming Soon
items.summary: I am in the “QE is coming soon” camp.
items.content_html:
I am in the “QE is coming soon” camp. Probably in January.

The Fed injected $29.4 billion of liquidity into the banking system on October 31st and another $13.5 billion on Monday.

Why do the banks lack liquidity? Two reasons. First, the banks gorged on Treasuries and MBS when Fed Funds was at zero in 2020 and 2021. Those securities largely sit as unrealized losses on bank balance sheets to this day (Bank of America, $BAC, case in point).

Second, the Fed took the bank reserve requirement down to zero percent in 2020 where it sits today. Bankers are like addicts, if you remove restraints, they will operate to the extreme and throw risk management out the window. Therefore, many banks do not have sufficient reserves on hand should customers come calling on deposits. Talk about moral hazard.

Expect the bailout economy to kick into high gear beginning in 2026. 2026 could be a year where GDP falls, yet unit prices moves higher on account of dovish monetary policy and yet more aggressive deficit spending on the fiscal side.

Washington D.C. desperately needs serious people at the Fed and in the White House. Something we have not had since Paul Volcker and Ronald Reagan. If you were to push back and say Calvin Coolidge was the last serious President we had from a fiscal standpoint, I would not argue.

items.title: Admins and defenders gird themselves against maximum-severity server vuln
items.summary: Open source React executes malicious code with malformed HTML—no authentication needed.
items.content_html:
Security defenders are girding themselves in response to the disclosure of a maximum-severity vulnerability disclosed Wednesday in React Server, an open-source package that’s widely used by websites and in cloud environments.

The vulnerability is easy to exploit and allows hackers to execute malicious code on servers that run it. Exploit code is now publicly available.

React is embedded into web apps running on servers so that remote devices render JavaScript and content more quickly and with fewer resources required. React is used by an estimated 6 percent of all websites and 39 percent of cloud environments. When end users reload a page, React allows servers to re-render only parts that have changed, a feature that drastically speeds up performance and lowers the computing resources required by the server.

items.title: Fraudulent gambling network may actually be something more nefarious
items.summary: Researchers say there's more to the network, which has operated for 14 years.
items.content_html:
A sprawling infrastructure that has been bilking unsuspecting people through fraudulent gambling websites for 14 years is likely a dual operation run by a nation-state-sponsored group that is targeting government and private-industry organizations in the US and Europe, researchers said Wednesday.

Researchers have previously tracked smaller pieces of the enormous infrastructure. Last month, security firm Sucuri reported that the operation seeks out and compromises poorly configured websites running the WordPress CMS. Imperva in January said the attackers also scan for and exploit web apps built with the PHP programming language that have existing webshells or vulnerabilities. Once the weaknesses are exploited, the attackers install a GSocket, a backdoor that the attackers use to compromise servers and host gambling web content on them.

All of the gambling sites target Indonesian-speaking visitors. Because Indonesian law prohibits gambling, many people in that country are drawn to illicit services. Most of the 236,433 attacker-owned domains hosting the gambling sites are hosted on Cloudflare. Most of the 1,481 hijacked subdomains were hosted on Amazon Web Services, Azure, and GitHub.
